newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares dived on a weak bullion price, which fixed in London at its lowest level in 20 months, shaving over two percent off the index.
Industrial shares retraced earlier losses ending a touch firmer, boosted by futures players in afternoon trade.

But dealers said trade was hampered for most of the day by the Johannesburg Equities Trading system which was initially shut down for three hours in the morning and again at 1310 GMT for the rest of the trading session following response problems.
"During the second halt which commenced at 1310 GMT it was decided to close the market for the remainder of the day," the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said in a statement.
It said this enabled the JSE to make further software changes prior to the start of trading on Tuesday.
Total trade for the day amounted to 318.4 million rand, compared with 390.5 million on Friday, the JSE said.
A trader said: "It has been an up and down day on the computer system."
Dealers said the market was bearish on a weak bullion price, which looked set to test support at $375 an ounce.

"The gold price is hovering on support at $375. There is no reason for the price to move up. Gold shares' performance is quite dismal and people are getting out of golds to have cash on hand," one said.

Industrial shares initially drifted lower on negative sentiment on fears of a correction on Wall Street as it has steamed higher and worries over a slower economic growth after a surprise interest rate hike last week, dealers said.
They said foreigners had kept to the sidelines for most of the day.
The market was seen continuing volatile on Tuesday on a weak bullion price and fears of a correction on Wall Street.
The gold index ended down 39.2 points or 2.36 percent to 1,621.3 points, pulling the all share index down 35.4 points to 6,691.3. The industrial index was up 2.8 points at 7,954.8.
Anglo lost 375 cents to 256 rand, Liberty Life shed 150 cents to 117.50 rand and Remgro gained 50 cents to 39.75 rand.
Dries shed 200 cents to 55 rand, Freegold dropped 125 cents to 37.75 rand, Kloof dumped 250 cents to 39.25 rand and Vaal Reefs lost 950 cents to 342.50 rand.
South African industrial equity industrial index futures reversed soft opening levels to end stronger on buying at lower levels. Gold contracts remained weak, weighed by a soft bullion price.
Dealers said the market would continue firm on Tuesday as there was still good demand for industrial and all-share contracts. Golds pinned their hopes on an improvement in the bullion price.
The December all-share contract was at 6,050/100 from 6,100, the gold contract was at 1,135/45 from 1,184 and the industrial contract at 7,665/12 from 7,636.
